title: The Scottish Administration (Offices) Order 2026
summary: This Order specifies the Clerk of the Sexual Offences Court and Deputy Clerks of the Sexual Offences Court as offices in the Scottish Administration which are not ministerial offices for the purposes of the Scotland Act 1998.

title: The School Teachers’ Pay and Conditions (England) Order 2026
summary: This Order makes provision for the determination of the remuneration of school teachers (within the meaning of section 122 of the Education Act 2002 (c. 32)) in England and other conditions of employment of school teachers which relate to their professional duties and working time.

title: The Scotland Act 1998 (Specification of Functions and Transfer of Property etc.) (Amendment) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the Scotland Act 1998 (Specification of Functions and Transfer of Property etc.) Order 2019 (S.I. 2019/183) (“the 2019 Order”) to remove reference to the Scottish Ministers’ functions under section 44 of the Climate Change (Scotland) Act 2009 (asp 12), because there are no functions under section 44 that could be exercised by way of arrangements under section 93 of the Scotland Act 1998 (c. 46).

title: The Building (Local Authority Charges and Amendments Relating to Charging) (England) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations set out provisions in relation to charges of local authorities for or in connection with certain building related functions.

title: The Air Navigation (Restriction of Flying) (Yorkshire Wildlife Park, South Yorkshire) (Emergency) (Revocation) Regulations 2026
The Welfare Food (Amendment) (England and Wales) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Welfare Food Regulations 1996 (S.I. 1996/1434) (“the 1996 Regulations”). The 1996 Regulations provide for a scheme (the “Nursery Milk Scheme”) which entitles children under the age of five years to one-third of a pint of milk (189ml) on any day where they are provided with childcare, by an approved childcare provider, for two hours or more. Regulations 3 to 10 amend the 1996 Regulations to replace references to day care with childcare and to update references to childcare legislation in England and Wales which have been updated since the 1996 Regulations came into force. These include changes made by the Childcare Act 2006 (c. 21) for England, and the Children and Families (Wales) Measure 2010 (nawm 1) and the Child Minding and Day Care Exceptions (Wales) Order 2010 (S.I. 2010/2839) (W.233)) for Wales. These Regulations also extend eligibility under the Nursery Milk Scheme to childcare providers registered with Childminder Agencies. Those providers will be able to claim reimbursement for milk they provide to eligible children in their care in the same way as childcare providers that are currently registered with Ofsted, or for providers registered with the Welsh Ministers in Wales. These Regulations also make provision in consequence of the repeal and replacement of the Child Minding and Day Care Exceptions (Wales) Order 2010 with the Child Minding and Day Care Exceptions (Revocation and Transitional Provision) (Wales) Order 2026 (S.I. 2026/100).

title: The Diocese of Leicester (Educational Endowments) (Hathern Church of England Primary School Teacher’s House) Order 2026
summary: This Order appoints the Leicester Diocesan Board of Education as trustee of the foundation known as Hathern Church of England Primary School Teacher’s House and makes new provision as to the use of that foundation. It creates a separate foundation for the purpose of providing religious education in accordance with the doctrines of the Church of England within the Parish of Hathern. The Order provides for the Religious Education Fund to be held on trust by the minister and churchwardens for the time being of the Parish of Hathern.

title: The Crime and Policing Act 2026 (Commencement No. 4) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations bring into force specified provisions of the Crime and Policing Act 2026 (c. 20) (“the Act”). These are the fourth commencement regulations made under the Act.

title: The Global Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law Sanctions (Overseas Territories) Order 2026
summary: This Order extends with modifications the Global Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law Sanctions Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/1071) (“the GHRIHLS Regulations”) as amended from time to time to all British overseas territories except Bermuda and Gibraltar (which implement sanctions under their own legislative arrangements).

title: The Port of Tyne Harbour Revision Order 2026
summary: This Order, made on the application of the Port of Tyne Authority, modernises and consolidates the statutory harbour powers which apply in relation to the Port of Tyne (‘the port’) and provides for—

title: The Inspectors of Education, Children’s Services and Skills (No. 3) Order 2026
summary: This Order appoints the persons named in the Schedule as His Majesty’s Inspectors of Education, Children’s Services and Skills.

title: The Housing (Empty Dwelling Management Orders) (Prescribed Period of Time and Prescribed Requirements) (England) (Amendment) Order 2026
summary: Chapter 2 of Part 4 of the Housing Act 2004 (c. 34) (“the Act”) deals with the making of interim and final empty dwelling management orders (“EDMOs) which may be made by local housing authorities in respect of dwellings which are wholly unoccupied.

title: The Tribunal Procedure (Upper Tribunal) (Amendment) Rules 2026
summary: These Rules amend the Tribunal Procedure (Upper Tribunal) Rules 2008 (S.I. 2008/2698), which govern the practice and procedure to be followed in the Upper Tribunal (other than the Lands Chamber of the Upper Tribunal), to—

title: The First-tier Tribunal and Upper Tribunal (Chambers) (Amendment No. 2) Order 2026
summary: The First-tier Tribunal and Upper Tribunal (Chambers) Order 2010 (S.I. 2010/2655) (“the 2010 Order”) organises the First-tier Tribunal and Upper Tribunal into chambers and makes provision for the allocation of those tribunals’ functions between the chambers.

title: The Income Tax (Pay As You Earn) (Amendment No. 3) Regulations 2026
summary:
These Regulations make amendments to the 
Income Tax (Pay As You Earn) Regulations 2003 (S.I. 2003/2682) (“the PAYE regulations”) to make loans and living accommodation a “specified benefit” for the purposes of Chapter 3A of the PAYE regulations and provide methods for calculating their cash equivalent or the relevant amount for the purposes of the PAYE regulations. This allows employers to apply to HMRC to become an “authorised employer” under regulation 61C of the PAYE regulations in respect of loans and living accommodation for the tax year 2027-28 onwards. These Regulations have no effect for the purposes of regulation 61C(4) and (5) (applications to become an authorised employer during a tax year) until the tax year 2027-28.

title: The Anti-social Behaviour (Provision of Information) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are made under section 105A of the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 (c. 12) (“the 2014 Act”), which enables the Secretary of State to make regulations placing a duty on specified authorities to provide the Secretary of State with specific information relating to anti-social behaviour. This may include information about reports of anti-social behaviour made to the authority, and their response to anti-social behaviour. Under section 105A(3), a relevant authority can be required to collect or obtain, create or produce, retain or process information in order to comply with this duty. A specified relevant authority for the purposes of these Regulations is a local authority (as defined in section 20 of the 2014 Act).

title: The Northern Ireland Assembly (Minimum Period) (Amendment) Order 2026
summary:
By virtue of 
section 31
(1) of the 
Northern Ireland Act 1998 (c. 47), ordinary general elections to the Northern Ireland Assembly are held on the first Thursday in May every five years. The predecessor Assembly must be dissolved at the start of the minimum period which ends with the date of the poll for the election and that period is determined in accordance with an Order made by the Secretary of State.

title: The Income-related Benefits (Subsidy to Authorities) Amendment Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the Income-related Benefits (Subsidy to Authorities) Order 1998 (S.I. 1998/562) (“the 1998 Order”) which provides for the calculation and payment of housing benefit subsidy to local authorities in England, Wales and Scotland which administer housing benefit. Sections 140C(4) and 140F(2) of the Social Security Administration Act 1992 (c. 5) authorise the making, revocation or varying of an Order before, during or after the year to which it relates.

title: The Licensing Act 2003 (Applications of Potential Strategic Importance to Greater London etc and Consequential Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: Section 51 of, and Schedule 26 to, the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 (c. 23) amended the Licensing Act 2003 (c. 17) by inserting powers enabling the Mayor of London to call in and determine certain licensing applications of potential strategic importance to Greater London. These Regulations supplement those provisions.

title: The Employment Appeal Tribunal (Amendment) (No. 2) Rules 2026
summary: These Rules amend the Employment Appeal Tribunal Rules 1993 (S.I. 1993/2854) (“the 1993 Rules”) which are the rules governing the procedure in the Employment Appeal Tribunal.
